title: 16-year-old with a year of progressive left foot twisting, hand tremor and slurred speech

provenance.citation: Synthetic case written 2026-10-17 for Rare Disease Detective; not derived from any individual patient.

chief_complaint: "My left foot has been twisting for a year and it's getting worse."
history_of_present_illness: One year of progressive left foot inversion while walking. Per the referral letter, symptoms are 'markedly worse in the mornings and improve as the day goes on.' Recently some slurring of speech noticed by friends and a decline in school grades. Occasional hand tremor when holding a cup.

symptom_timeline.event: Left foot inversion, worst late in the afternoon per mother's account
Hand tremor when holding a cup

movement_findings.observation: Left foot dystonic inversion on walking.
Bilateral postural and action tremor of the hands with a proximal, coarse 'wing-beating' quality on arm abduction.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Mildly slowed processing; inappropriate jocularity noted
neurological_exam.reflexes: Referral letter: 'normal'. Clinic exam: 3+ at knees bilaterally
neurological_exam.other: Slit-lamp examination not documented in the referral. Abdomen not examined at this visit. Examined at 3 PM.

imaging.report: Summary line: 'Normal study.' Findings section: 'Symmetric T2 hyperintensity in the bilateral putamina and thalami.'

family_history: Older sister had 'unexplained hepatitis' at age 14.
social_history: Year 11 student; grades dropped from mostly A's to C's over the past year, teachers report he is 'distracted and silly in class'. Lives with parents and older sister. Denies alcohol, smoking, or drugs; parents agree. No medications.
prior_workup_and_opinions: Referral letter: 'Probable dopa-responsive dystonia; Wilson excluded; please start levodopa.'
